newsitem.title: USA: Okla. taxpayers sue bond firms on "yield burning".
newsitem.headline: Okla. taxpayers sue bond firms on "yield burning".

text.p: Ten Oklahoma taxpayers have charged in state court that four bond dealers allegedly made over $1.2 million in secret profits on deals for Oklahoma City and a state water resources board in 1993 and 1994.

The two lawsuits, filed in November and December 1996, appear to be the second and third actions ever by a state or local government against bond dealers focusing on a controversial market practice dubbed "yield burning."
Defendants named in the November challenge are Stifel, Nicolaus and Co.; Dillon Read & Co; Leo Oppenheim & Co; and A.G. Edwards & Sons Inc, according to court papers.
A.G. Edwards & Sons is owned by A.G. Edwards Inc..
Also named in the November action were Oklahoma City and Robert Cochran, a former investment banker with Stifel, Nicolaus.

Defendants named in the December lawsuit are Cochran; his former employer Stifel, Nicolaus; the Oklahoma Water Resources Board; board trustee Boatmen's First National Bank of Oklahoma; Bayerische Landesbank Girozentrale, a foreign bank where the plaintiffs contend that secret funds were placed; and a person named Chris Cochran.

The $1.3 trillion municipal bond market has been rocked by charges of yield burning -- where bond underwriters allegedly overcharge issuers for U.S. Treasuries bought in the open market and used in bond refinancing transactions.
The December 17 lawsuit alleges that Stifel secretly overcharged the state water board roughly $459,000 for U.S. Treasuries that were needed to redeem, at market price, the refunded bonds.
The lawsuit also charges Stifel with misconduct during a competitive bid for an investment contract used in the December financing.
